Entering data

Writing in a cell

ActionEffect
type on a selected cellreplaces its content
double click, F2 or Enteredits its content
Enterconfirms and moves down one cell
click in another cellconfirms
Escabandons the entry
Alt Enternew line inside the cell
Delete or ⌫empties the selected cells, including checkboxes and drop-down lists; their formatting stays
right-click › Clear contentthe same

While typing, the arrow keys move the caret in the text. Otherwise the arrow keys, Tab and Shift Tab change cells.

What DocCells recognizes

You typeYou get
12, -3, 1e5a number, aligned right
2.5a decimal number; the separator is the decimal point
25%, 2.5%a percentage
2026-11-25, 2026/11/25a date
2026-11-25 14:30a date and a time
TRUE, FALSEa logical value
[2, 1]a list
=A1+B1a formula
anything elsetext, aligned left

Dates

A date is typed year first: 2026-11-25. 11/25/2026 stays a text, which cannot be calculated with. To display it as usual, choose Format › Number › Date (11/29/2017) or a custom format.

A double click on a date cell opens a calendar. =TODAY() gives today's date.

Texts made of digits

A number starting with zero loses that zero: 007 becomes 7. To keep it, first give the cells the Plain text format (Format › Number › Plain text), or start with an apostrophe: '007.

Common entry problems

You seeCause
a number aligned leftit is a text: a decimal comma, a unit (12 $), an extra space
46351 instead of a datea date in the Automatic format: give it the Date format
the text cut off by the next cellwiden the column, or choose Wrap

For a unit, enter the number alone and give it a format: currency, or a custom one such as 0.00 "m".
